claims.text: Nanostructured tungsten carbide can serve as an effective catalyst for both HER and HOR.
Tungsten carbide has a platinum-like electronic structure.
Tungsten carbide has superior resistance to corrosive, high-temperature environments.
Conventional carburization of tungsten precursors can produce high-surface-area nanostructured tungsten carbide.
The proposed WC catalyst is to be integrated into an electrochemical cell and evaluated under acidic or otherwise harsh fuel-cell conditions.
Acidic electrolytes and elevated temperatures are typical operating conditions for the relevant fuel-cell or electrolyzer environments.
The WC crystal structure provides catalytically active surface sites.
The electronic configuration of WC surface sites mimics that of platinum.
The platinum-like electronic configuration of WC facilitates favorable hydrogen adsorption and desorption kinetics.
The d-band electronic structure of WC adjusts hydrogen adsorption energy to values favorable for both HER and HOR.
The chemical stability of WC under corrosive conditions improves long-term catalyst durability.
Nanostructured WC will exhibit lower overpotentials than untreated materials.
Nanostructured WC will exhibit improved kinetic parameters, including reduced Tafel slopes, relative to untreated materials.
Nanostructured WC will undergo less catalytic-activity degradation during prolonged operation.
WC performance can be meaningfully benchmarked against platinum catalysts and untreated WC electrodes under identical conditions.
The proposed benefit is limited to electrocatalytic systems exposed to severe acidic and high-temperature conditions.
The magnitude of WC performance improvement over platinum-based catalysts under specific HER and HOR conditions is uncertain.
